messages.author: 12303b3baa6498f6
messages.subject: Delete the alometry effect
parts:
Hi community, I found that the alometry effect in my data was significant and the proportion of variance that explains this factor is around 11%. I used the function plotAlometry and procD.lm with the method RegScore to check if the shape differences are just a manifestation of shape allometry. I check that the shape differences are not a manifestation of shape allometry therefore I see the effect for species too, but my director wants that I delete this effect. The users of morphoJ use the residuals of multivariate regression to delete the alometry effect but I don't know how I can do this in R.

 Any help is welcome. Thanks

messages.author: fbfd20ce829c6c6c
messages.subject: Re: [geomorph-r-package] Delete the alometry effect
parts:
Hi Emanuel, 

To be clear, are you saying that you have found evidence of common allometry for each of your species? (e.g., an insignificant interaction term in a model of Shape ~ Size * Species). If so, then you can extract residuals from this multivariate regression simply by using the resid() function on the model fit produced by procD.lm(). 

However, if there is no evidence for a common allometry for each of your species (a significant Size:Species interaction term), then obtaining residuals from this model to account for size and for use in downstream analyses is not recommended. Instead, one might consider explicitly incorporating size in a model, rather than removing its effect using the residual approach you described.

Best,
Bryan
